answer: Each new identity must pass a wharf queue before its first work counts, finishing a sequential puzzle chain that takes ten minutes on one processor, each step feeding the next and the chain signed by the claimant, so it cannot be split across machines. A falcon verifier checks the chain within an hour; a copied step, duplicate chain, or failed signature discards the work and blocks it, wasting that effort. One honest agent pays ten minutes once, while a thousand fakes cost ten thousand minutes, and copying a relic credential buys no entry.
